key_insight: Marginal Advantage Accumulation (MAA) turns noisy batch-by-batch memory feedback into stable cross-batch evidence so truly useful operations can be identified and reinforced.
engineering_relevance: For memory-driven agents, MAA offers a practical post-processing layer that improves trace distillation robustness without changing the base model or requiring expensive online optimization.
method: Build comparable differential signals across batches
Accumulate signed per-operation evidence with EMA
Merge semantically identical traces to preserve cross-batch identity
evidence_signal: Across 4 benchmarks and 4 target models, the paper reports best results in 14 of 16 settings and about 75% lower optimization-phase token consumption versus batch-level baselines.
watch_item: Semantic identity merging and evidence accumulation depend on reliable trace matching, so noisy operation descriptions or inconsistent labeling could weaken gains.
paper_title: Marginal Advantage Accumulation for Memory-Driven Agent Self-Evolution
